# Physiology, MHC Class I

**Authors:** Matthew Becar, Anup Kasi

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I is a diverse set of cell surface receptors expressed on all nucleated cells in the body and platelets. MHC is also known as human leukocyte antigen (HLA), of which there are 3 subtypes: HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C. These molecules play a vital role in the immune system recognizing self from nonself, presenting foreign antigens to other immune cells. HLA class I alleles are extremely polymorphic among the world population, which presents issues relating to human tissue transplants.
